The screen-space error metric selects the closest point, reducing "aura" artifacts [S1][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that the screen-space error metric selects the 'closest point'. However, the evidence explicitly states that the metric selects the point with the 'smallest unbounding sphere radius, as measured in screen-space' (Source [S1] Section 3.2, Source [S3] Section 3.2). Selecting the point with the smallest screen-space error (smallest radius relative to distance) is not equivalent to selecting the geometrically closest point (smallest t value). In fact, the algorithm tracks a 'candidate_t' and updates it only if the current 'error' is lower than the previous best, which may result in selecting a point further away if it has a smaller screen-space error. Therefore, the specific mechanism described in the claim ('selects the closest point') is factually incorrect according to the evidence.
